To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hemolysis is a serious problem in many hemolytic diseases including SCD, PNH and drug-induced hemolysis.
hemolysis is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with hemolytis diseases.
hemolytic diseases are associated with a number and variety of symptoms, including hemoglobinuria, hypertension, hypercoagulation, and erectile dysfunction.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (i) How does hemolysis affect the cardiovascular system? (ii) What is the role of cell-free hemolysate in the pathophysiology of hemolytic disorders? and (iii) What are the mechanisms that lead to hemolytic complications?
understanding the pathophysiology of hemolysis, in particular the role of cell-free Hbs in the development of complications in patients with hemolytically active diseases.
the pathophysiological consequences of excessive hemolysis, which is a serious complication of many inherited and acquired diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pathophysiological consequences of cell-free hemolysis in hemolytic diseases are much more serious than it was previously thought.
hemolytic diseases are not just hemolytic diseases but also diseases associated with hemolysis.

the pathophysiology of diseases associated with hemolysis is complex and is related to a number of mechanisms including: (1) hemoglobinemia, (2) hemoglobinuria, (3) oxidative stress and prooxidant effects of Hb, (4) NO scavenging, (5) proinflammatory and procoagulant effects of Hb.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the pathophysiology of the consequences of hemolyses in the patients with hemolytis diseases is very complex and is not fully understood yet, but it seems to be very promising that new therapeutic strategies will be developed.
cell-free Hb, in particular in the presence of heme, is a potent pathogen, responsible for a number of complications observed in patients with hemolytis.
cell-free Hb plays an important role in the pathophysiology of hemolytic disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pathophysiological consequences of excessive hemolysis are much more than hemoglobinemia.
the hemolytic diseases should be treated as a systemic condition, and not just a local problem.
the role of hemolysate in the pathophysiology of hemolytic disorders should be considered as a major factor in the design of new therapies for these patients.
